question: Some studies found overweight people outlived those of normal weight. Which correction shrank that advantage the most?
options: Excluding smokers and the already ill
answer: Excluding smokers and the already ill. Smoking and hidden disease make people thinner and kill them sooner, dragging down the survival of the normal-weight group. Pooling millions of never-smokers without known disease, the Global BMI Mortality Collaboration found the lowest death rates at a BMI of 20 to 25. Thinness can be a symptom.
move: When the thin die sooner, ask what made them thin.
ask: When a surprising finding flatters my habits, have I asked what else could explain it?
trap: BMI counts muscle as fat, so separating them seems the fix.
source: Global BMI Mortality Collaboration, The Lancet, 2016
reference: The Global BMI Mortality Collaboration, Body-mass index and all-cause mortality: individual-participant-data meta-analysis of 239 prospective studies in four continents, The Lancet, 2016
